features.feature: Skip-link contrast on bespoke-CSS surfaces (cascade specificity)
features.user_story: As a keyboard user landing on any page — including the bespoke passthrough pages — I can read the skip link when it takes focus.
features.expected: `.skip-link` renders its designed inverted chip (background var(--ink), text var(--bg)) on EVERY surface. No page-level stylesheet may out-specify the shell rule and repaint the chip's text, and the rendered pair must meet WCAG 1.4.3 at >=4.5:1.

This is the worst ratio the ledger has recorded and the only finding to date where the text is not merely low-contrast but literally invisible — a sighted keyboard user sees the accent focus ring land on a blank cream box. NOT a colour bug: `--bg` resolves correctly to #060606 at every level of the chain (verified by walking the ancestor chain: A.skip-link / BODY.phase0 / HTML.dark-mode all report #060606). It is a specificity bug. Three rules set colour on this element — `a {color:inherit}` (0,0,1) in tokens.css, `.skip-link {color:var(--bg)}` (0,1,0) in shell.css, and `.phase0 a {color:inherit}` (0,1,1) in phase0.css. The last wins on specificity and hands the chip back the inherited body cream. Scope is exactly one page: /brand/, the other bespoke-CSS surface, carries no blanket `a` rule and measured clean. Missed by every prior run because the skip link sits at left:-999px in its resting state, so a sweep that filters to on-screen elements never measures it — this run caught it by measuring every element with layout geometry regardless of viewport position. | /phase0/ skip link re-measured live 2026-08-25: still rgba(243,240,232,.82) on its own cream chip = 1.00:1, the worst ratio in the ledger and still literally invisible to a sighted keyboard user. features.feature: Image-plate scrim — the darkening gradient did not cover a title tall enough to reach the top of the plate
features.user_story: As a reader scanning the archive, I can read the white title on every image plate, however long the title is and whichever texture the plate drew.
features.expected: .plate-image::after paints a black scrim over the texture so the white .plate-title clears WCAG AA large-text (3:1) everywhere the title can actually land — not only in the bottom band that justify-content: flex-end targets.

features.p2: ISSUE/High (2026-09-06) — the scrim is `linear-gradient(to top, rgba(0,0,0,.78), rgba(0,0,0,.08) 55%, rgba(0,0,0,.14))`: .78 black at the bottom, but only .08–.14 across the top ~45%. That is sound while every title fits inside the bottom band, which is what `justify-content: flex-end` assumes. It does not hold for a three-line Anton title: 'Show Me Your Glory' is 165px tall in a 283px plate, so flex-end has no free space left to give and the first line starts 7% from the top. On `.img-concrete`, whose texture opens on a #c7c7c7 band, the white cap-height rows of 'SHOW' sit on a measured rgb(158,158,158) — 2.68:1 against a 3:1 large-text floor. 'The Theology of Staying on the Call' fails the same way at 2.92:1. Six of the eight live image plates pass (img-lines worst 3.69:1, img-noise worst 12.27:1), so this is texture-and-title-length dependent, not universal. MEASUREMENT: rasterised the homepage in headless Chrome at 1280 wide with the Earlier section unhidden, then sampled a glyph-free 12px strip inside each plate at each glyph row and took the row median — the computed-style probe reports 1.06:1 for all eight, which is the known .plate-image artifact and is why nine months of sweeps saw nothing. This is the second time that artifact has hidden a real defect (F100 was the first) and the first time it hid one in PRODUCTION rather than on /brand/.
features.p3: FIX (qa/fixes-20260906) — css/plates.css:216-235: the scrim's upper stops go .08/.14 -> .26/.34; the .78 bottom is untouched, so the gradient keeps its bottom-heavy reveal and the textures still read. Chosen over darkening .img-concrete's #c7c7c7 top band because the scrim is the thing that is supposed to guarantee legibility, and fixing it there covers every texture and any future one. The change is monotonic — the new alpha is >= the old at every point of the gradient — so no element anywhere on the site can lose contrast from it. Parity carried in the same commit per the dogfood contract (F87/F99/F100): brand/brand.css:870-877 mirrors the new stops, and DESIGN-SYSTEM.md Sec.09 updates both the code block and the prose that quoted '.14 at the top'.
